title: The Cosmic Opening and the First Draft
paragraphs: §The Life-Light
Before anything existed—before the universe, before time itself—the Word was already there. The Word was face to face with God, and the Word was God. He was with God, ready and present, from day one.

Everything was created through him. Not a single thing—nothing!—came into being without him. What came into existence was Life itself, and that Life was Light for everyone to live by. The Life-Light blazed out into the darkness, and the darkness couldn't put it out.

There was a man named John, sent by God to point everyone toward the Life-Light. His job was to show people where to look and who to believe in. John wasn't the Light himself—he was just there to point the way to the Light.

The Life-Light was the real deal: everyone who steps into Life, he brings into Light. He was right here in the world—the world that was made through him—and yet the world didn't even notice him. He came to his own people, but they didn't want him. But everyone who did want him, everyone who believed he was who he claimed to be and trusted he would do what he said—he gave them their true selves, their child-of-God selves. These are God-born people, not born by blood or human desire or anyone's decision.

Then the ultimate plot twist: The Word became flesh and blood and moved into our neighborhood. We saw his glory with our own eyes—the one-of-a-kind glory, like Father, like Son—generous inside and out, true from start to finish.
John pointed him out and shouted, "This is the One! The One I told you was coming after me but is actually ahead of me. He has always been ahead of me—he always gets the first word."

We all live off his endless generosity—gift after gift after gift. We got the basics from Moses, and then this overflowing giving and receiving, this endless knowing and understanding of God—all of it came through Jesus, the Messiah. No one has ever seen God, not even a glimpse. But this one-of-a-kind God-Expression, who lives at the very heart of the Father, has made him as plain as day.
§Thunder in the Desert

When the religious leaders in Jerusalem sent a group of priests and officials to ask John who he was, he didn't dodge. He was completely straight with them. He told the plain truth: "I am not the Messiah."
They pressed him: "Then who are you? Elijah?" "I'm not." "The Prophet?" "No."
Frustrated, they said, "Then who ARE you?! We need an answer to take back to the people who sent us. Tell us something—anything—about yourself!"
"I'm thunder in the desert: 'Make the road straight for God!' I'm doing exactly what the prophet Isaiah said would happen."
The interrogation squad was from the Pharisee party, and they had their own question: "If you're not the Messiah, not Elijah, and not the Prophet—then why are you baptizing people?!"

John answered, "I only baptize with water. But right here among you is standing someone you don't even recognize. He comes after me, but he's not second place to me—I'm not even worthy to hold his coat for him."
(All of these conversations happened in Bethany on the other side of the Jordan River, where John was baptizing at the time.)
§The God-Revealer

The very next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and yelled out, "Here he is—God's Passover Lamb! He takes away the sin of the world! This is the man I've been telling you about: 'the One who comes after me but is really ahead of me.' I didn't know who he was at first—I only knew my job: to get Israel ready to recognize him as the God-Revealer. That's why I came baptizing with water, giving you a good bath, scrubbing the sins from your life so you can get a fresh start with God."

John backed up his testimony with this: "I watched the Spirit come down out of the sky like a dove and make himself at home in him. I keep telling you, I knew nothing about him except this: The One who sent me to baptize with water told me, 'The One you see the Spirit come down and stay on—that's the One who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.' That's exactly what I saw happen, and I'm telling you straight: there is zero doubt about it. THIS is the Son of God."
§Come, See for Yourself
The next day John was back at his post with two of his disciples watching. He looked up, saw Jesus walking nearby, and said, "Here he is—God's Passover Lamb."
The two disciples heard him and went after Jesus. Jesus looked over his shoulder and said to them, "What are you after?" They said, "Rabbi" (which means "Teacher"), "where are you staying?"
He replied, "Come along and see for yourself." They came, saw where he was staying, and ended up hanging out with him for the rest of the day. It was late afternoon when this happened.

Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who heard John's testimony and followed Jesus. The first thing he did after finding where Jesus lived was track down his own brother Simon, telling him, "We've found the Messiah!" (that is, "Christ"). He brought him straight to Jesus. Jesus took one look at him and said, "You're Simon, John's son? From now on your name is Cephas" (or Peter, which means "Rock").
The next day Jesus decided to head for Galilee. When he got there, he ran into Philip and said, "Come, follow me." (Philip's hometown was Bethsaida—same town as Andrew and Peter.)

Philip went and found Nathanael and told him, "We've found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets preached about. It's Jesus, Joseph's son, the one from Nazareth!" Nathanael said, "Nazareth? You've got to be kidding." But Philip said, "Come and see for yourself."
When Jesus saw him coming he said, "There's a real Israelite—not a single fake bone in his body."
Nathanael said, "Where did you get that idea? You don't even know me." Jesus answered, "One day, long before Philip called you over here, I saw you under the fig tree."
Nathanael exclaimed, "Rabbi! You are the Son of God, the King of Israel!"

Jesus said, "You became a believer just because I said I saw you sitting under the fig tree one day? You haven't seen anything yet! Before this is over, you're going to see heaven ripped open and God's angels going up and down on the Son of Man."

title: The Wedding Crash and the Temple Whip
paragraphs: §From Water to Wine

Three days later there was a wedding in the village of Cana in Galilee. Jesus' mother was there, and Jesus and his disciples were guests too. When the wine started running low at the wedding banquet, Jesus' mother told him, "They're just about out of wine."
Jesus said, "Is that any of our business, Mother—yours or mine? This isn't my time. Don't push me."
She went ahead anyway, telling the servants, "Whatever he tells you, do it."

Six stoneware water pots were sitting there, used by the Jews for ritual washings. Each one held twenty to thirty gallons. Jesus ordered the servants, "Fill the pots with water." And they filled them right to the brim.
"Now fill your pitchers and take them to the host," Jesus said, and they did.

When the host tasted the water that had become wine (he had no idea what had just happened, but the servants knew, of course), he called the bridegroom over. "Everybody I know starts with the finest wines, and after the guests have had plenty, brings out the cheap stuff. But you've saved the best for last!"
This act in Cana of Galilee was the first sign Jesus gave—the first glimpse of his glory. And his disciples believed in him.
After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples, and stayed there for several days.
§Tear Down This Temple . . .

When the Passover Feast, celebrated each spring by the Jews, was about to take place, Jesus traveled up to Jerusalem. He found the Temple teeming with people selling cattle and sheep and doves. The loan sharks were there in full force too.

Jesus put together a whip out of strips of leather and chased them all out of the Temple—stampeding the sheep and cattle, flipping over the tables of the loan sharks, spilling coins left and right. He told the dove merchants, "Get your stuff out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a shopping mall!" That's when his disciples remembered the Scripture: "Zeal for your house consumes me."

But the Jews were upset. They demanded, "What credentials can you show us to prove you have the right to do this?" Jesus answered, "Tear down this Temple, and in three days I'll put it back together."

They were furious: "It took forty-six years to build this Temple, and you're going to rebuild it in three days?!" But Jesus was talking about his body as the Temple. Later, after he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered he had said this. Then it clicked, and they believed both what was written in Scripture and what Jesus had said.

During the time he was in Jerusalem, those days of the Passover Feast, lots of people saw the signs he was doing and, seeing they pointed straight to God, entrusted their lives to him. But Jesus didn't entrust his life to them. He knew them inside and out—knew how untrustworthy they were. He didn't need anyone's help to see right through them.

title: The Midnight Meeting and the Famous Verse
paragraphs: §Born from Above

So, there was this guy named Nicodemus, a super important religious leader (a Pharisee) among the Jewish people. One night, pretty late, he came to visit Jesus. He said, "Rabbi, we all know you're a teacher sent directly from God. Nobody could do all these amazing, God-revealing things you're doing unless God was totally with you."
Jesus replied, "You're spot on. Seriously, listen up: Unless someone is 'born from above,' they can't even begin to understand what I'm talking about—they can't see God's kingdom."

Nicodemus was totally confused. "How can anyone be born again once they're already grown up? You can't just climb back into your mom's womb! What are you even talking about with this 'born from above' thing?"

Jesus said, "You're not really listening. Let me break it down again. Unless a person totally gives in to this original creation—you know, like when the 'wind hovered over the water' at the very beginning, the invisible stuff moving the visible stuff, a kind of baptism into a brand new life—it's impossible to actually enter God's kingdom. When you look at a baby, it's just a body you can see and touch. But the real person taking shape inside is formed by something you can't see or touch—that's the Spirit—and that's what makes them a living spirit."

"So, don't be so shocked when I tell you that you've got to be 'born from above'—like, out of this world, if that makes sense. You totally get how the wind blows wherever it wants. You can hear it rustling through the trees, but you have no clue where it came from or where it's going next. That's exactly how it is for everyone who is 'born from above' by the wind of God, the Spirit of God."
Nicodemus asked, "Wait, what do you even mean by this? How does any of this actually happen?"

Jesus responded, "You're a respected teacher in Israel, and you don't even know these basic things? Listen carefully. I'm telling you the honest truth. I'm only talking about what I know firsthand, from my own experience; I'm only testifying to what I've seen with my own eyes. There's no secondhand info here, no rumors. Yet, instead of just looking at the evidence and accepting it, you're just stalling with questions. If I tell you things that are super obvious, right in front of your face, and you don't believe me, what's the point of telling you about things you can't see, the deep things of God?"

"Nobody has ever gone up into God's presence except the One who came down from that Presence, the Son of Man. It's like how Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the desert so people could look at it and believe they'd be healed (Numbers 21:8-9). In the same way, the Son of Man has to be lifted up— and everyone who looks up to him, truly trusting and expecting, will get a real life, an eternal life."

"Here's how much God totally loved the world: He gave his Son, his one and only Son. And this is why: so that no one ever has to be destroyed; by believing in him, anyone can have a complete and lasting life. God didn't go through all that trouble of sending his Son just to point fingers and tell the world how messed up it was. He came to help, to fix the world up again. Anyone who trusts in him is declared innocent; anyone who refuses to trust him has actually been under a death sentence for a long time without even realizing it. And why? Because that person failed to believe in the one-of-a-kind Son of God when they were introduced to him."

"This is the major crisis we're facing: God's light streamed into the world, but people everywhere just ran for the darkness. They chose the darkness because they weren't genuinely interested in making God happy. Everyone who constantly does evil, who's hooked on denial and living in an illusion, hates God's light and won't come anywhere near it, scared of being painfully exposed. But anyone who works and lives in truth and reality totally welcomes God's light so that their work can be seen for the God-work it truly is."
§The Bridegroom's Friend

After this whole conversation, Jesus went with his disciples into the Judean countryside and hung out with them there. He was also baptizing people. At the same time, John (the Baptist) was also baptizing over at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there. This was all happening before John got thrown into jail. John's disciples actually got into a big argument with some of the religious leaders (the establishment Jews) about what baptism really meant. So, they went to John and said, "Rabbi, you know that guy who was with you on the other side of the Jordan? The one you vouched for with your testimony? Well, he's basically competing with us now. He's baptizing too, and everyone is going to him instead of us!"

John answered, "It's just not possible for a person to succeed—and I'm talking about real, eternal success—without help from heaven. You yourselves were right there when I publicly announced that I wasn't the Messiah but simply the one sent ahead of him to get things ready. The guy who gets the bride is, by definition, the bridegroom. And the bridegroom's friend, his 'best man'—that's me—standing right there by his side where he can hear every word, is genuinely thrilled. How could he possibly be jealous when he knows the wedding is happening and the marriage is off to a great start?"
"That's why my cup is overflowing with joy. This is the exact moment for him to move into the spotlight, while I quietly step off to the sidelines."

"The One who comes from above is way above all other messengers from God. Someone born on earth is limited to earth and speaks earth-language; but the One born from heaven is in a league of his own. He lays out the proof of what he saw and heard in heaven. But seriously, no one really wants to deal with these facts. Yet, anyone who truly examines this evidence will eventually stake their whole life on this: that God himself is the truth."

"The One that God sent speaks God's actual words. And don't think for a second that he rations out the Spirit in tiny bits and pieces. The Father loves the Son like crazy, extravagantly. He handed everything over to him so he could give it away—a super generous distribution of gifts. That's why whoever accepts and trusts the Son gets in on everything, a life that's complete and lasts forever! And that's also why the person who avoids and distrusts the Son is totally in the dark and doesn't see life. All they experience of God is darkness, and a really angry darkness at that."

title: The Woman at the Well and the Long-Distance Miracle
paragraphs: §The Woman at the Well

Jesus realized that the Pharisees were keeping score of the baptisms he and John were doing (although it was actually his disciples, not Jesus himself, doing the baptizing). They had posted the score: Jesus was ahead, turning him and John into rivals in people's eyes. So Jesus left the Judean countryside and headed back to Galilee.

To get there, he had to go through Samaria. He came to Sychar, a Samaritan village near the field Jacob had given his son Joseph. Jacob's well was still there. Jesus, worn out from the trip, sat down by the well. It was about noon.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus said, "Would you give me a drink of water?" (His disciples had gone into the village to buy food for lunch.)
The Samaritan woman was taken aback. "How come you, a Jew, are asking me, a Samaritan woman, for a drink?" (Jews in those days wouldn't be caught dead talking to Samaritans.)
Jesus answered, "If you knew the generosity of God and who I am, you would be asking me for a drink, and I would give you fresh, living water."

The woman said, "Sir, you don't even have a bucket, and this well is deep. So how are you going to get this 'living water'? Are you greater than our ancestor Jacob, who dug this well and drank from it—he and his sons and his livestock—and passed it down to us?"

Jesus said, "Everyone who drinks this water will get thirsty again and again. But anyone who drinks the water I give will never thirst—not ever. The water I give will become an artesian spring inside them, gushing fountains of endless life."
The woman said, "Sir, give me this water so I'll never get thirsty and never have to come back to this well again!"
He said, "Go call your husband and come back."

"I have no husband," she said. "That's a nice way to put it: 'I have no husband.' You've had five husbands, and the man you're living with now isn't even your husband. You told the truth there, that's for sure."
"Oh, so you're a prophet! Well, tell me this: Our ancestors worshiped God on this mountain, but you Jews say Jerusalem is the only place to worship, right?"

"Believe me, woman, the time is coming when you Samaritans will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. You worship guessing in the dark; we Jews worship in the clear light of day. God's way of salvation comes through the Jews. But the time is coming—in fact, it's already here—when what you're called won't matter and where you worship won't matter either.

"It's who you are and how you live that count before God. Your worship has to engage your spirit in the pursuit of truth. That's the kind of people the Father is looking for: people who are simply and honestly themselves before him in worship. God is sheer being—Spirit. Those who worship him must do it from their very being, their spirits, their true selves, in adoration."
The woman said, "I don't know about all that. But I do know the Messiah is coming. When he gets here, we'll get the whole story."
"I am he," said Jesus. "You don't have to wait any longer or look any further."
Just then his disciples came back. They were shocked—they couldn't believe he was talking with that kind of woman. No one said what they were all thinking, but their faces showed it.

The woman took the hint and left. In her confusion she left her water jar behind. Back in the village she told the people, "Come see a man who knew everything I ever did, who knows me inside and out! Do you think this could be the Messiah?" And they went out to see for themselves.
§It's Harvest Time
In the meantime, the disciples kept urging him, "Rabbi, eat! Aren't you going to eat?"
He told them, "I have food to eat that you know nothing about."
The disciples were confused. "Who could have brought him food?"

Jesus said, "The food that keeps me going is doing the will of the One who sent me, finishing the work he started. Look around right now—wouldn't you say it's about four months until harvest? Well, I'm telling you, open your eyes and take a good look at what's right in front of you. These Samaritan fields are ripe. It's harvest time!

"The Harvester isn't waiting. He's already taking his pay, gathering this grain that's ripe for eternal life. Now the Sower is arm in arm with the Harvester, celebrating. That's the truth behind the saying, 'One person sows, another harvests.' I sent you to harvest a field you never worked. Without lifting a finger, you've walked into a field that others worked long and hard."

Many Samaritans from that village believed in him because of the woman's testimony: "He knew everything I ever did—he knows me inside and out!" They asked him to stay, so Jesus stayed two days. A lot more people believed when they heard what he had to say. They told the woman, "We don't believe just because of what you said anymore. We've heard it for ourselves and we know for sure: He is the Savior of the world!"

After the two days he left for Galilee. Jesus knew from experience that a prophet gets no respect in his hometown. So when he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him—but only because they were impressed by what he had done in Jerusalem during the Passover Feast, not because they really understood who he was or what he was up to.

Now he was back in Cana of Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. Meanwhile, in Capernaum there was a royal official whose son was sick. When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die. Jesus pushed back: "Unless you people see a miracle, you refuse to believe."
But the official wouldn't take no for an answer. "Sir, come down! It's life or death for my son!"
Jesus simply said, "Go home. Your son lives." The man believed Jesus' bare word and headed home. On the way, his servants met him with the news: "Your son lives!"
He asked them when he had started to get better. They said, "The fever broke yesterday at one in the afternoon." The father realized that was the exact moment Jesus had said, "Your son lives."
That settled it. Not only he but his entire household believed. This was the second sign Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.

title: The Pool of Bethesda and the Boss Claim
paragraphs: §Even on the Sabbath

Soon another feast came around and Jesus was back in Jerusalem. Near the Sheep Gate there was a pool—in Hebrew called Bethesda—with five alcoves. Hundreds of sick people—blind, crippled, paralyzed—were lying in these alcoves. One man had been an invalid there for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him stretched out by the pool and knew how long he had been there, he said, "Do you want to get well?"
The sick man said, "Sir, when the water is stirred, I don't have anybody to put me in the pool. By the time I get there, somebody else is already in."
Jesus said, "Get up, take your bedroll, start walking." The man was healed on the spot. He picked up his bedroll and walked off.
That day happened to be the Sabbath. The Jews stopped the healed man and said, "It's the Sabbath. You can't carry your bedroll around. It's against the rules."
But he told them, "The man who made me well told me to. He said, 'Take your bedroll and start walking.'"
They asked, "Who gave you the order to pick it up and start walking?" But the healed man didn't know, because Jesus had slipped away into the crowd.
A little later Jesus found him in the Temple and said, "You look wonderful! You're well! Don't go back to a sinning life, or something worse might happen."
The man went back and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. That is why the Jews were out to get Jesus—because he did this kind of thing on the Sabbath.
But Jesus defended himself. "My Father is working straight through, even on the Sabbath. So am I."

That really set them off. The Jews were now not just out to expose him—they were out to kill him. Not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was calling God his own Father, putting himself on the same level as God.
§What the Father Does, the Son Does

So Jesus explained himself at length. "I'm telling you straight: The Son can't do a thing on his own, only what he sees the Father doing. What the Father does, the Son does. The Father loves the Son and includes him in everything he is doing.

"But you haven't seen the half of it yet. In the same way that the Father raises the dead and creates life, so does the Son. The Son gives life to anyone he chooses. Neither he nor the Father shuts anyone out. The Father handed all authority to judge over to the Son, so that the Son will be honored equally with the Father. Anyone who dishonors the Son dishonors the Father, because it was the Father's decision to put the Son in the place of honor.

"It's urgent that you listen carefully to this: Anyone here who believes what I am saying right now and aligns himself with the Father—who has, in fact, put me in charge—has at this very moment the real, lasting life and is no longer condemned to be an outsider. This person has taken a giant step from the world of the dead into the world of the living.

"It's urgent that you get this right: The time has arrived—I mean right now!—when dead men and women will hear the voice of the Son of God and, hearing, will come alive. Just as the Father has life in himself, he has given the Son life in himself. And he has given him the authority, simply because he is the Son of Man, to decide and carry out matters of judgment.

"Don't act so surprised at all this. The time is coming when everyone dead and buried will hear his voice. Those who have lived the right way will walk out into a resurrection Life; those who have lived the wrong way, into a resurrection Judgment.

"I can't do a single thing on my own: I listen, then I decide. You can trust my decision because I'm not out to get my own way—I'm only here to carry out orders. If I were just speaking on my own, it would be an empty, self-serving testimony. But there is another witness who confirms me, the most reliable Witness of all. Besides, you all saw and heard John, and he gave expert, reliable testimony about me, didn't he?

"But I'm not trying to win your vote, and I'm not appealing to human testimony. I'm telling you this so that you will be saved. John was a torch, blazing and bright, and you were happy to dance in his bright light for an hour or so. But the testimony that really confirms me far exceeds John's. It's the work the Father gave me to finish. These very tasks, as I go about completing them, confirm that the Father did send me. The Father who sent me confirmed me. And you missed it. You never heard his voice, you never saw his face. There's nothing left in your memory of his message, because you don't take his Messenger seriously.

"You have your heads in your Bibles constantly because you think you'll find eternal life there. But you miss the forest for the trees. These Scriptures are all about me! And here I am, standing right in front of you, and you aren't willing to receive from me the life you say you want.

"I'm not interested in crowd approval. And do you know why? Because I know you and your crowds. I know that love—especially God's love—is not on your agenda. I came with my Father's authority, and you either dismiss me or avoid me. If someone else came, acting self-important, you'd welcome him with open arms. How do you expect to get anywhere with God when you spend all your time competing with each other for position, ranking your rivals and ignoring God?

"But don't think I'm going to accuse you before my Father. Moses, in whom you put so much stock, is your accuser. If you really believed what Moses said, you would believe me—he wrote about me. If you won't take seriously what he wrote, how can I expect you to take seriously what I say?"

title: The Ultimate Catering Miracle and the Hard Truth
paragraphs: §Bread and Fish for All

After this, Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee (some call it Tiberias). A huge crowd followed him, drawn by the miracles they had seen him do among the sick. When he got to the other side, he climbed a hill and sat down with his disciples around him. It was nearly time for the Passover Feast, which the Jews kept every year.

When Jesus looked up and saw that a massive crowd had arrived, he said to Philip, "Where can we buy bread to feed all these people?" He said this to stretch Philip's faith—he already knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered, "Two hundred silver pieces wouldn't buy enough bread for each person to get even a bite."
One of the disciples—it was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother—said, "There's a little boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But that's a drop in the bucket for a crowd like this."

Jesus said, "Make everyone sit down." There was a nice carpet of green grass there. They sat down—about five thousand of them. Then Jesus took the bread, gave thanks, and gave it to those who were seated. He did the same with the fish. Everyone ate as much as they wanted.
When they had eaten their fill, he told his disciples, "Gather the leftovers so nothing goes to waste." They got to work and filled twelve large baskets with leftovers from the five barley loaves.

The people realized God was at work among them in what Jesus had just done. They said, "This is the Prophet for sure—God's Prophet, right here in Galilee!" Jesus saw that in their excitement they were about to grab him and force him to be king, so he slipped away back up the mountain by himself.

In the evening his disciples went down to the sea, got into a boat, and headed back across the water to Capernaum. It had grown quite dark and Jesus still hadn't come back. A huge wind blew up, churning the sea. They were maybe three or four miles out when they saw Jesus walking on the sea, quite close to the boat. They were scared out of their minds, but he reassured them: "It's me. It's all right. Don't be afraid." So they took him on board, and in no time they reached land—the exact spot they were headed to.

The next day, the crowd that had stayed behind realized there had been only one boat, and that Jesus had not gotten into it with his disciples—they had seen them leave without him. By now boats from Tiberias had pulled up near where they had eaten the bread the Master had blessed. So when the crowd realized he was gone and wasn't coming back, they piled into the Tiberias boats and headed for Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
When they found him on the other side of the sea, they said, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"
Jesus answered, "You've come looking for me not because you saw God in what I did, but because I fed you, filled your stomachs—and for free.

"Don't waste your energy chasing food that goes bad. Work for the food that sticks with you, food that nourishes your lasting life—food the Son of Man provides. He and what he does are guaranteed by God the Father to last."
§The Bread of Life
To that they said, "Well, what do we have to do to get in on God's work?"
Jesus said, "Sign on with the One God has sent. That kind of commitment gets you in on God's work."

They waffled: "Why don't you give us a clue about who you are—just a hint of what's going on? When we see what's up, we'll commit. Show us what you can do. Moses fed our ancestors with bread in the desert. The Scriptures say: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"

Jesus responded, "The real point of that Scripture isn't that Moses gave you bread from heaven—it's that my Father is right now offering you bread from heaven, the real bread. The Bread of God came down out of heaven and is giving life to the world."
They jumped at that: "Master, give us this bread, now and forever!"

Jesus said, "I am the Bread of Life. The person who aligns with me will never hunger and never thirst, ever. I've told you this straight, because even though you've seen me in action, you don't really believe me. Everyone the Father gives me eventually comes running to me. And once that person is with me, I hold on and don't let go. I came down from heaven not to follow my own agenda but to do the will of the One who sent me.

"This, in a nutshell, is that will: everything the Father handed over to me gets completed—not a single detail missed—and at the wrap-up of time I have everything and everyone put together, whole and upright. This is what my Father wants: anyone who sees the Son and trusts who he is and what he does, and aligns with him, will enter real life, eternal life. My part is to put them on their feet, alive and whole, at the completion of time."

At this, because he said, "I am the Bread that came down from heaven," the Jews started arguing about him: "Isn't this Joseph's son? Don't we know his father? Don't we know his mother? How can he say, 'I came down out of heaven,' and expect anyone to believe him?"

Jesus said, "Don't bicker about me among yourselves. You're not in charge here—the Father who sent me is in charge. He draws people to me; that's the only way you'll ever come. Only then do I do my work: putting people together, setting them on their feet, ready for the End. This is what the prophets meant when they wrote, 'And then they will all be personally taught by God.' Anyone who has spent any time listening to the Father—really listening, and therefore learning—comes to me to be taught personally. To see it with his own eyes, hear it with his own ears, from me, since I got it firsthand from the Father. No one has seen the Father except the One who shares being with the Father—and you can see me.

"I'm telling you the most solemn truth: Whoever believes in me has real, eternal life. I am the Bread of Life. Your ancestors ate the manna in the desert and died. But here is Bread that truly comes down out of heaven. Anyone who eats this Bread will never die. I am the Bread—living Bread!—who came down out of heaven. Anyone who eats this Bread will live, and forever! The Bread I present to the world, so it can eat and live, is myself—this flesh-and-blood self."
At this, the Jews started fighting among themselves: "How can this man serve up his flesh as a meal?"

But Jesus didn't back down an inch. "Only as you eat and drink flesh and blood—the flesh and blood of the Son of Man—do you have life in you. The one who brings a hearty appetite to this eating and drinking has eternal life and will be fit and ready for the Final Day. My flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. By eating my flesh and drinking my blood, you enter into me and I into you. Just as the fully alive Father sent me and I live because of him, so the one who makes a meal of me lives because of me. This is the Bread from heaven. Your ancestors ate bread and later died. Whoever eats this Bread will live forever."
He said these things while teaching in the meeting place in Capernaum.
§Too Tough to Swallow
Many of his disciples heard this and said, "This is tough teaching—too tough to swallow."

Jesus sensed his disciples were struggling with this and said, "Does this completely rattle you? What would happen if you saw the Son of Man going up to where he came from? The Spirit is what gives life. Sheer muscle and willpower don't make anything happen. Every word I've spoken to you is a Spirit-word, and so it creates life. But some of you are resisting, refusing to have any part in this." (Jesus knew from the start who wasn't going to risk themselves with him. He also knew who would betray him.) He went on: "This is why I told you earlier that no one can come to me on his own. You get to me only as a gift from the Father."
After this, many of his disciples left. They didn't want to be associated with him anymore. Then Jesus gave the Twelve their chance: "Do you want to leave too?"
Peter replied, "Master, who would we go to? You have the words of real, eternal life. We've already committed ourselves, confident that you are the Holy One of God."

Jesus responded, "Haven't I handpicked you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!" He was talking about Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. This man—one of the Twelve!—was already getting ready to betray him.

title: Undercover at the Festival
paragraphs: Later Jesus was going about his business in Galilee. He didn't want to travel in Judea because the Jews there were looking for a chance to kill him. It was nearly time for Tabernacles, a feast the Jews kept every year.

His brothers said, "Why don't you leave here and go up to the Feast so your disciples can get a good look at the works you do? No one who wants to be publicly known does everything behind the scenes. If you're serious about what you're doing, come out in the open and show the world." His brothers were pushing him like this because they didn't believe in him either.

Jesus shot back, "Don't pressure me. This isn't my time. It's your time—it's always your time; you have nothing to lose. The world has nothing against you, but it's up in arms against me. It's against me because I expose the evil behind its pretensions. You go ahead, go up to the Feast. Don't wait for me. I'm not ready. It's not the right time for me."

He said this and stayed on in Galilee. But later, after his family had gone up to the Feast, he went too. But he kept out of the way, careful not to draw attention to himself. The Jews were already out looking for him, asking around, "Where is that man?"

There was a lot of heated talk about him buzzing through the crowds. Some were saying, "He's a good man." But others said, "No way. He's a con artist." This kind of talk went on in hushed whispers because people were scared of the intimidating Jewish leaders.
§Could It Be the Messiah?
With the Feast already half over, Jesus showed up in the Temple, teaching. The Jews were impressed but puzzled: "How does he know so much without going to school?"

Jesus said, "I didn't make this up. What I teach comes from the One who sent me. Anyone who wants to do his will can test this teaching and know whether it's from God or whether I'm making it up. A person who makes things up tries to make himself look good. But someone trying to honor the one who sent him sticks to the facts and doesn't mess with reality. It was Moses, wasn't it, who gave you God's Law? But not one of you is living it. So why are you trying to kill me?"
The crowd said, "You're crazy! Who's trying to kill you? You must be demon-possessed."

Jesus said, "I did one miraculous thing a few months ago, and you're still standing around upset, wondering what I'm up to. Moses prescribed circumcision—though it actually came from his ancestors, not Moses—and so you circumcise a man, dealing with one part of his body, even on the Sabbath. You do this to keep one item of Moses' Law. So why are you upset with me because I made a man's entire body well on the Sabbath? Don't be hypercritical. Use your head—and your heart!—to figure out what's right, to test what's genuinely right."

That's when some of the Jerusalem locals said, "Isn't this the guy they wanted to kill? And here he is out in the open, saying whatever he wants, and nobody's stopping him. Could it be that the rulers actually know he is the Messiah? But wait—we know where this man is from. The Messiah is going to come out of nowhere. Nobody will know where he's from."

That set Jesus off, and he cried out while teaching in the Temple: "So you think you know me and where I'm from—but that's not where I'm from. I didn't set myself up in business. My true origin is in the One who sent me, and you don't know him at all. I come from him—that's how I know him. He sent me here."

They were looking for a way to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, because it wasn't God's time yet. Many in the crowd put their faith in him, saying, "When the Messiah comes, will he give better or more convincing evidence than this?"

The Pharisees, alarmed at this rebellious undercurrent running through the crowd, teamed up with the high priests and sent their police to arrest him. Jesus brushed them off: "I'm only with you a short time. Then I go to the One who sent me. You will look for me, but you won't find me. Where I am, you can't come."

The Jews huddled together. "Where do you think he's going that we won't be able to find him? Is he about to go to the Greek world to teach the Jews there? What is he talking about: 'You will look for me, but you won't find me,' and 'Where I am, you can't come'?"

On the final, climactic day of the Feast, Jesus stood up and cried out: "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink. Rivers of living water will brim and spill out of the depths of anyone who believes in me this way, just as the Scripture says." (He said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were about to receive. The Spirit hadn't been given yet, because Jesus hadn't been glorified yet.)

Those in the crowd who heard these words were saying, "This has to be the Prophet." Others said, "He is the Messiah!" But others said, "The Messiah doesn't come from Galilee, does he? Don't the Scriptures say the Messiah comes from David's line and from Bethlehem, David's village?" So the crowd was split over him. Some even wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.
Then the Temple police reported back to the high priests and Pharisees, who demanded, "Why didn't you bring him in?"
The police answered, "Have you heard the way he talks? We've never heard anyone speak like this man."

The Pharisees said, "Are you brainwashed like the rest of the rabble? Do you see any of the leaders believing in him? Any of the Pharisees? It's only this crowd, ignorant of God's Law, that's taken in by him—and they're damned."
Nicodemus—the man who had come to Jesus earlier, who was both a ruler and a Pharisee—spoke up. "Does our Law condemn a man without first listening to him and finding out what he's doing?"
But they cut him off. "Are you campaigning for the Galilean too? Check the evidence. See if any prophet ever comes from Galilee." Then they all went home.

title: The Trap, The Light, and the Ultimate Mic Drop
paragraphs: §To Throw the Stone
Jesus went across to the Mount of Olives, but he was soon back in the Temple again. Crowds of people swarmed to him. He sat down and taught them.

The religion scholars and Pharisees dragged in a woman who had been caught in the act of adultery. They stood her in plain sight of everyone and said, "Teacher, this woman was caught red-handed in adultery. Moses, in the Law, orders us to stone people like this. What do you say?" They were trying to trap him into saying something they could charge him with.

Jesus bent down and wrote with his finger in the dirt. They kept pushing, badgering him. He straightened up and said, "The sinless one among you, go first: throw the stone." Then he bent down again and kept writing in the dirt.
Hearing that, they walked away one by one, starting with the oldest. The woman was left alone. Jesus stood up and spoke to her. "Woman, where are they? Does no one condemn you?"
"No one, Master." "Neither do I," said Jesus. "Go on your way. From now on, don't sin." (Note: John 7:53–8:11 — this story isn't in the earliest handwritten copies of John's Gospel.)
§You're Missing God in All This
Jesus addressed them again: "I am the world's Light. No one who follows me stumbles around in the dark. I give plenty of light to live in."
The Pharisees objected, "All we have is your word for this. We need more than that to go on."

Jesus replied, "You're right that you only have my word—but you can trust it's true. I know where I came from and where I'm going next. You don't know where I'm from or where I'm headed. You judge by what you can see and touch. I don't judge like that. But even if I did, my judgment would be true, because I wouldn't make it from the narrowness of my experience but from the largeness of the One who sent me, the Father. That meets the conditions in God's Law: you can count on the testimony of two witnesses. And that's what you have—you have my word, and you have the word of the Father who sent me."

They said, "Where is this so-called Father of yours?" Jesus said, "You're looking right at me and you don't see me. How do you expect to see the Father? If you knew me, you'd know the Father at the same time."
He gave this speech in the Treasury while teaching in the Temple. No one arrested him, because his time wasn't up yet.
Then he went over the same ground again. "I'm leaving, and you're going to look for me—but you're missing God in all this, and you're headed for a dead end. There's no way you can come with me."
The Jews said, "So is he going to kill himself? Is that what he means by 'you can't come with me'?"

Jesus said, "You're tied down to the ordinary; I'm in touch with what's beyond your horizons. You live by what you see and touch. I'm living on other terms. I told you you're missing God in all this. You're at a dead end. If you won't believe I am who I say I am, you're at the dead end of sins. You're missing God in your lives."

They said to him, "Just who are you, anyway?" Jesus said, "What I've been saying from the start. I have so much to say about you, judgments that affect you—but if you don't trust the One who gave me my words and actions, none of it matters. It's him you're questioning, not me—the One who sent me."

They still didn't get it—didn't realize he was talking about the Father. So Jesus tried again. "When you lift up the Son of Man, then you'll know who I am—that I'm not making this up, but speaking only what the Father taught me. The One who sent me stays with me. He doesn't abandon me. He sees how much joy I take in pleasing him."
When he put it like that, many people decided to believe.
§If the Son Sets You Free

Then Jesus turned to the Jews who claimed to believe in him. "If you stick with this, living out what I tell you, you are truly my disciples. Then you'll experience the truth for yourselves, and the truth will set you free."
Surprised, they said, "But we're descendants of Abraham. We've never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, 'The truth will set you free'?"

Jesus said, "I tell you solemnly: anyone who chooses a life of sin is trapped in a dead-end life and is, in fact, a slave. A slave can't come and go as he pleases. The Son, though, has a permanent place—the run of the house. So if the Son sets you free, you are free through and through. I know you're Abraham's descendants. But I also know you're trying to kill me, because my message hasn't gotten through your thick skulls yet. I'm talking about things I've seen while keeping company with the Father, and you just keep doing what you've heard from your father."

They were indignant. "Our father is Abraham!" Jesus said, "If you were Abraham's children, you'd be doing what Abraham did. But here you are trying to kill me—a man who's told you the truth he got straight from God! Abraham never did anything like that. You keep repeating the works of your father." They said, "We're not illegitimate children. We have a legitimate father: the one and only God."

"If God were your father," said Jesus, "you'd love me, because I came from God and arrived here. I didn't come on my own—he sent me. Why can't you understand a word I say? Here's why: you can't handle it. You're from your father, the Devil, and all you want to do is please him. He was a killer from the very start. He couldn't stand the truth, because there wasn't a shred of truth in him. When the Liar speaks, he makes it up out of his lying nature and fills the world with lies. I show up, tell you the plain truth, and you want nothing to do with me. Can any of you convict me of a single misleading word, a single sinful act? But if I'm telling the truth, why don't you believe me? Anyone on God's side listens to God's words. That's why you're not listening—because you're not on God's side."
§I Am Who I Am
The Jews shot back, "That settles it. We were right all along calling you a Samaritan and saying you're crazy—demon-possessed!"

Jesus said, "I'm not crazy. I simply honor my Father, while you dishonor me. I'm not trying to get anything for myself. God has something gloriously grand in mind here and is making the decisions to bring it about. I say this with total confidence: if you practice what I'm telling you, you'll never have to look death in the face."

At this the Jews said, "Now we know you're crazy. Abraham died. The prophets died. And you show up saying, 'If you practice what I'm telling you, you'll never face death—not even a taste.' Are you greater than Abraham, who died? The prophets died too! Who do you think you are!"

Jesus said, "If I were trying to grab all the attention, it wouldn't amount to anything. But my Father—the same One you call your Father—put me here in this moment of splendor. You haven't recognized him in this. But I have. If I, in false modesty, said I didn't know what was going on, I'd be as much of a liar as you are. But I do know, and I'm doing what he says. Abraham—your 'father'—with joyful faith looked down the corridors of history and saw my day coming. He saw it and cheered."
The Jews said, "You're not even fifty years old—and Abraham saw you?"
"Believe me," said Jesus, "I am who I am, long before Abraham was anything."
That did it—pushed them over the edge. They picked up rocks to throw at him. But Jesus slipped away, getting out of the Temple.

title: Spit, Mud, and the Blind Guy Who Roasted the Pharisees
paragraphs: §True Blindness
Walking down the street, Jesus saw a man blind from birth. His disciples asked, "Rabbi, who sinned—this man or his parents—to make him born blind?"

Jesus said, "You're asking the wrong question. You're looking for someone to blame. There's no such cause-and-effect here. Look instead for what God can do. We need to be hard at work for the One who sent me here, working while the sun shines. When night falls, the workday is over. As long as I am in the world, there is plenty of light. I am the world's Light."

He said this, then spit in the dust, made a clay paste with the saliva, rubbed the paste on the blind man's eyes, and said, "Go, wash at the Pool of Siloam" (Siloam means "Sent"). The man went and washed—and saw.
Soon the town was buzzing. His relatives and the people who year after year had seen him as a blind beggar were saying, "Isn't this the man we knew, who sat here begging?"
Others said, "It's him, all right!" But others objected, "It's not the same man at all. He just looks like him." He said, "It's me—the very one."
They said, "How did your eyes get opened?"
"A man named Jesus made a paste, rubbed it on my eyes, and told me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' I did what he said. When I washed, I saw."
"So where is he?" "I don't know."

They marched the man to the Pharisees. This day when Jesus made the paste and healed his blindness was the Sabbath. The Pharisees grilled him again on how he had come to see. He said, "He put a clay paste on my eyes, and I washed, and now I see."

Some of the Pharisees said, "Obviously, this man can't be from God. He doesn't keep the Sabbath." Others countered, "How can a bad man do miraculous, God-revealing things like this?" There was a split in their ranks.
They came back at the blind man: "You're the expert. He opened your eyes. What do you say about him?" He said, "He is a prophet."

The Jews didn't believe it—didn't believe the man had been blind in the first place. So they called the parents of the man, now bright-eyed with sight. They asked, "Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he now sees?"

His parents said, "We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind. But we don't know how he came to see—we have no clue who opened his eyes. Why don't you ask him? He's a grown man and can speak for himself." (His parents talked like this because they were intimidated by the Jewish leaders, who had already decided that anyone who stood up for this man as the Messiah would be kicked out of the meeting place. That's why his parents said, "Ask him. He's a grown man.")
They called the man back a second time—the man who had been blind—and told him, "Give credit to God. We know this man is a fraud."
He replied, "I know nothing about that one way or the other. But I know one thing for sure: I was blind… I now see."
They said, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
"I've told you over and over and you haven't listened. Why do you want to hear it again? Are you dying to become his disciples?"
With that they jumped all over him. "You might be a disciple of that man, but we're disciples of Moses. We know for sure God spoke to Moses, but we have no idea where this man even comes from."

The man replied, "This is amazing! You claim to know nothing about him, but the fact is, he opened my eyes! Everyone knows God doesn't take orders from sinners, but listens carefully to anyone who lives in reverence and does his will. That someone opened the eyes of a man born blind has never been heard of—ever. If this man didn't come from God, he couldn't do a thing."
They said, "You're nothing but dirt! How dare you talk to us like that!" Then they threw him out into the street.
Jesus heard they'd thrown him out, and went and found him. He asked, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
The man said, "Point him out to me, sir, so I can believe in him."
Jesus said, "You're looking right at him. Don't you recognize my voice?"
"Master, I believe," the man said, and worshiped him.

Jesus then said, "I came into the world to bring everything into clear daylight, making all the distinctions sharp—so that those who have never seen will see, and those who put on a great show of seeing will be exposed as blind."
Some Pharisees overheard him and said, "Does that mean you're calling us blind?"
Jesus said, "If you were really blind, you'd be blameless. But since you claim to see everything so well, you're accountable for every fault and failure."

title: The Good Shepherd and the Hanukkah Showdown
paragraphs: §He Calls His Sheep by Name

"Let me put this before you as plainly as I can. If someone climbs over or through the fence of a sheep pen instead of going through the gate, you know he's up to no good—a sheep rustler! The shepherd walks right up to the gate. The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep recognize his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out. When he's gotten them all out, he leads them, and they follow because they're familiar with his voice. They won't follow a stranger's voice—they'll scatter, because they don't recognize the sound."

Jesus told them this simple story, but they had no idea what he was talking about. So he tried again. "I'll be explicit, then. I am the Gate for the sheep. All those others are up to no good—sheep rustlers, every one of them. But the sheep didn't listen to them. I am the Gate. Anyone who goes through me will be cared for—will freely go in and out, and find pasture. A thief is only there to steal and kill and destroy. I came so they can have real, eternal life—more and better life than they ever dreamed of.

"I am the Good Shepherd. The Good Shepherd puts the sheep before himself, sacrificing himself if necessary. A hired man is not a real shepherd. The sheep mean nothing to him. He sees a wolf coming and runs for it, leaving the sheep to be torn apart and scattered by the wolf. He's only in it for the money. The sheep don't matter to him.

"I am the Good Shepherd. I know my own sheep, and my own sheep know me. In the same way, the Father knows me and I know the Father. I put the sheep before myself, sacrificing myself if necessary. You need to know that I have other sheep besides the ones in this pen. I need to gather and bring them too. They'll also recognize my voice. Then it will be one flock, one Shepherd. This is why the Father loves me: because I freely lay down my life. And so I am free to take it up again. No one takes it from me. I lay it down of my own free will. I have the right to lay it down, and I also have the right to take it up again. I received this authority personally from my Father."

This kind of talk caused another split in the Jewish ranks. Many of them were saying, "He's crazy, a maniac—completely out of his head. Why bother listening to him?" But others weren't so sure: "These aren't the words of a crazy man. Can a 'maniac' open blind eyes?"

They were celebrating Hanukkah just then in Jerusalem. It was winter. Jesus was strolling in the Temple across Solomon's Porch. The Jews circled him and said, "How long are you going to keep us guessing? If you're the Messiah, tell us straight out."

Jesus answered, "I told you, but you don't believe. Everything I've done has been authorized by my Father—actions that speak louder than words. You don't believe because you're not my sheep. My sheep recognize my voice. I know them, and they follow me. I give them real, eternal life. They are protected from the Destroyer for good. No one can steal them out of my hand. The Father who put them under my care is far greater than the Destroyer and Thief. No one could ever get them away from him. I and the Father are one heart and mind."
Again the Jews picked up rocks to throw at him. Jesus said, "I've given you, as a gift from the Father, a great many good actions. For which of these acts are you stoning me?"
The Jews said, "We're not stoning you for anything good you did, but for what you said—this blasphemy of calling yourself God."

Jesus said, "I'm only quoting your inspired Scriptures, where God said, 'I tell you—you are gods.' If God called your ancestors 'gods'—and Scripture doesn't lie—why do you yell, 'Blasphemer! Blasphemer!' at the unique One the Father set apart and sent into the world, just because I said, 'I am the Son of God'? If I don't do the things my Father does, fine—don't believe me. But if I am doing them, set aside for a moment what you hear me say about myself and just take the evidence of the actions right before your eyes. Then maybe things will come together for you, and you'll see that not only are we doing the same thing, we are the same—Father and Son. He is in me; I am in him."

They tried yet again to arrest him, but he slipped through their fingers. He went back across the Jordan to the place where John first baptized, and stayed there. Many people followed him there. They were saying, "John did no miracles, but everything he said about this man has come true." Many believed in him right then and there.

title: The Ultimate Flex (Raising the Dead)
paragraphs: §The Death of Lazarus

A man was sick—Lazarus of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. This was the same Mary who massaged the Lord's feet with fragrant oils and then wiped them with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was sick. So the sisters sent word to Jesus: "Master, the one you love so much is sick."
When Jesus got the message, he said, "This sickness won't end in death. It will become a chance to show God's glory by glorifying God's Son."

Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. But oddly, when he heard Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was for two more days. After the two days, he said to his disciples, "Let's go back to Judea."
They said, "Rabbi, you can't do that. The Jews are out to kill you, and you're going back?"

Jesus replied, "Aren't there twelve hours of daylight? Anyone who walks in daylight doesn't stumble, because there's plenty of light from the sun. Walking at night, he might well stumble, because he can't see where he's going."
He said these things, and then announced, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. I'm going to wake him up."
The disciples said, "Master, if he's asleep, he'll get good rest and wake up fine." Jesus was talking about death, while his disciples thought he meant taking a nap.
Then Jesus was blunt: "Lazarus died. And I'm glad for your sakes that I wasn't there. You're about to get new reasons to believe. Now let's go to him."
That's when Thomas, the one called the Twin, said to his companions, "Come on. We might as well die with him."

When Jesus finally got there, he found Lazarus already four days dead. Bethany was near Jerusalem, only a couple of miles away, and many of the Jews were visiting Martha and Mary, sympathizing with them over their brother. Martha heard Jesus was coming and went out to meet him. Mary stayed in the house.
Martha said, "Master, if you'd been here, my brother wouldn't have died. Even now, I know that whatever you ask God, he will give you."
Jesus said, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha replied, "I know he'll rise again in the resurrection at the end of time."

"You don't have to wait for the End. I am, right now, Resurrection and Life. The one who believes in me, even though he dies, will live. And everyone who lives believing in me doesn't ultimately die at all. Do you believe this?"
"Yes, Master. All along I've believed you are the Messiah, the Son of God who comes into the world."
After saying this, she went to her sister Mary and whispered in her ear, "The Teacher is here and is asking for you."

The moment she heard that, she jumped up and ran out to him. Jesus hadn't yet entered the town but was still at the place where Martha had met him. When her sympathizing Jewish friends saw Mary run off, they followed, thinking she was heading to the tomb to weep there. Mary came to where Jesus was waiting and fell at his feet, saying, "Master, if only you'd been here, my brother wouldn't have died."
When Jesus saw her sobbing, and the Jews with her sobbing, a deep anger welled up inside him. He said, "Where did you put him?"
"Master, come and see," they said. Now Jesus wept.
The Jews said, "Look how deeply he loved him."
Others among them said, "Well, if he loved him so much, why didn't he do something to keep him from dying? After all, he opened the eyes of a blind man."

Then Jesus, anger welling up inside him again, arrived at the tomb. It was a simple cave in the hillside with a slab of stone laid against it. Jesus said, "Remove the stone." Martha, the dead man's sister, said, "Master, by now there's a stench. He's been dead four days!"
Jesus looked her in the eye. "Didn't I tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?"

Then, to the others: "Go ahead, take away the stone." They removed the stone. Jesus raised his eyes to heaven and prayed, "Father, I'm grateful that you've listened to me. I know you always listen, but because of this crowd standing here I've said this out loud, so they might believe you sent me."
Then he shouted, "Lazarus, come out!" And he came out—a dead man, wrapped from head to toe, with a cloth over his face. Jesus told them, "Unwrap him and let him loose."
§The Man Who Creates God-Signs

That was a turning point for many of the Jews who were with Mary. They saw what Jesus did and believed in him. But some went back to the Pharisees and reported on Jesus. The high priests and Pharisees called a meeting of the Jewish ruling body. "What do we do now?" they asked. "This man keeps doing things, creating God-signs. If we let him go on, pretty soon everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away what little power and privilege we still have."

Then one of them—Caiaphas, the designated Chief Priest that year—spoke up: "Don't you know anything? Can't you see it's to our advantage that one man dies for the people rather than the whole nation being destroyed?" He didn't say this on his own; as Chief Priest that year he unknowingly prophesied that Jesus was about to die as a sacrifice for the nation—and not only for the nation, but so that all God's scattered, exiled children might be gathered into one people.

From that day on, they plotted to kill him. So Jesus no longer went out in public among the Jews. He withdrew into the countryside bordering the desert, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there quietly with his disciples.

The Jewish Passover was coming up. Crowds were making their way from the countryside up to Jerusalem to get ready for the Feast. They were curious about Jesus. There was a lot of talk about him among those standing around in the Temple: "What do you think? Will he show up at the Feast or not?"
Meanwhile, the high priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where he was should report it. They were all set to arrest him.

title: The Perfume, The Traitor, and The Parade
paragraphs: §Anointing His Feet

Six days before Passover, Jesus entered Bethany, where Lazarus—so recently raised from the dead—was living. Lazarus and his sisters invited Jesus to dinner at their home. Martha served. Lazarus was one of those sitting at the table with them. Mary came in with a jar of very expensive fragrant oil, anointed and massaged Jesus' feet, and then wiped them with her hair. The fragrance of the oil filled the house.

Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples—even then getting ready to betray him—said, "Why wasn't this oil sold and the money given to the poor? It would easily have brought three hundred silver pieces." He said this not because he cared two cents about the poor, but because he was a thief. He was in charge of their shared money, but he also skimmed from it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She's getting ready for the day of my burial, and honoring it. You always have the poor with you. You don't always have me."

Word got out among the Jews that he was back in town. People came to take a look—not only at Jesus, but also at Lazarus, who had been raised from the dead. So the high priests plotted to kill Lazarus, because so many of the Jews were crossing over and believing in Jesus on account of him.
§See How Your King Comes

The next day the huge crowd that had arrived for the Feast heard Jesus was entering Jerusalem. They broke off palm branches and went out to meet him. And they cheered: Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in God's name! Yes! The King of Israel! Jesus got a young donkey and rode it, just as the Scripture says: Don't be afraid, Daughter Zion: see how your king comes, riding a donkey's colt.
The disciples didn't catch the fulfillment of many Scriptures at the time, but after Jesus was glorified, they remembered that what was written about him matched what was done to him.

The crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb, raising him from the dead, was there giving eyewitness accounts. It was because they'd spread the word of this latest God-sign that the crowd had swelled into a welcome parade. The Pharisees took one look and threw up their hands: "It's out of control. The whole world is stampeding after him."
§A Grain of Wheat Must Die
There were some Greeks in town who had come up to worship at the Feast. They approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee: "Sir, we want to see Jesus. Can you help us?"
Philip went and told Andrew. Andrew and Philip together told Jesus. Jesus answered, "Time's up. The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

"Listen carefully: unless a grain of wheat is buried in the ground, dead to the world, it never becomes more than a grain of wheat. But if it's buried, it sprouts and reproduces itself many times over. In the same way, anyone who clings to life exactly as it is destroys that life. But if you let it go, reckless in your love, you'll have it forever—real and eternal.
"If any of you wants to serve me, then follow me. Then you'll be where I am, ready to serve at a moment's notice. The Father will honor and reward anyone who serves me.

"Right now I am shaken. And what am I going to say—'Father, get me out of this'? No—this is why I came in the first place. I'll say, 'Father, put your glory on display.'" A voice came out of the sky: "I have glorified it, and I'll glorify it again."
The listening crowd said, "Thunder!" Others said, "An angel spoke to him!"

Jesus said, "The voice didn't come for me—it came for you. Right now the world is in crisis. Now Satan, the ruler of this world, will be thrown out. And I, as I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to me and gather them around me." He said it this way to show how he was going to die.
Voices from the crowd answered, "We heard from God's Law that the Messiah lasts forever. How can it be necessary, as you put it, for the Son of Man to 'be lifted up'? Who is this 'Son of Man'?"

Jesus said, "For a little while longer, the light is among you. Walk by the light you have, so darkness doesn't destroy you. If you walk in darkness, you don't know where you're going. While you have the light, believe in the light. Then the light will be inside you, shining through your lives. You'll be children of light."
§Their Eyes Are Blinded

Jesus said all this, and then went into hiding. All these God-signs he had shown them, and they still didn't get it—still wouldn't trust him. This proved the prophet Isaiah was right: God, who believed what we preached? Who recognized God's arm, stretched out and ready to act? First they wouldn't believe, then they couldn't—again, just as Isaiah said: Their eyes are blinded, their hearts are hardened, so they wouldn't see with their eyes and understand with their hearts, and turn to me, God, so I could heal them.
Isaiah said these things after he got a glimpse of God's overflowing glory that would pour through the Messiah.

On the other hand, quite a few of the leaders did believe. But because of the Pharisees, they didn't say so openly. They were afraid of being kicked out of the meeting place. When push came to shove, they cared more about human approval than God's glory.

Jesus summed it all up when he cried out, "Whoever believes in me believes not just in me but in the One who sent me. Whoever looks at me is really looking at the One who sent me. I am Light that has come into the world, so that everyone who believes in me won't have to stay in the dark any longer.

"If anyone hears what I'm saying and doesn't take it seriously, I don't reject him. I didn't come to reject the world—I came to save the world. But you need to know that whoever brushes me off, refusing to take in what I'm saying, is deliberately choosing rejection. The Word—the Word-made-flesh that I have spoken and that I am—that Word and no other is the final word. I'm not making any of this up on my own. The Father who sent me gave me orders—told me what to say and how to say it. And I know exactly what his command produces: real, eternal life. That's all I have to say. What the Father told me, I tell you."

title: Dirty Feet and the Setup
paragraphs: §Washing His Disciples' Feet

Just before the Passover Feast, Jesus knew the time had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his dear companions, he kept loving them right to the end. It was suppertime. By now the Devil had Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, firmly in his grip, all set for the betrayal.

Jesus knew the Father had put him in complete charge of everything—that he came from God and was on his way back to God. So he got up from the supper table, set aside his robe, and put on an apron. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet, drying them with his apron. When he got to Simon Peter, Peter said, "Master—you wash my feet?"
Jesus answered, "You don't understand now what I'm doing, but it'll be clear to you later."
Peter persisted, "You're not going to wash my feet—ever!" Jesus said, "If I don't wash you, you can't be part of what I'm doing."
"Master!" said Peter. "Then not only my feet. Wash my hands! Wash my head!"

Jesus said, "If you've had a bath in the morning, you only need your feet washed now, and you're clean from head to toe. My concern, you understand, is holiness, not hygiene. So now you're clean. But not every one of you." (He knew who was betraying him. That's why he said, "Not every one of you.") After he'd finished washing their feet, he took his robe, put it back on, and went back to his place at the table.

Then he said, "Do you understand what I've done for you? You call me 'Teacher' and 'Master,' and rightly so—that's what I am. So if I, the Master and Teacher, washed your feet, you must now wash each other's feet. I've laid down a pattern for you. What I've done, you do. I'm only pointing out the obvious: a servant isn't ranked above his master; an employee doesn't give orders to the employer. If you understand what I'm telling you, act like it—and live a blessed life.
§The One Who Ate Bread at My Table

"I'm not including all of you in this. I know exactly whom I've chosen, so as not to interfere with this Scripture coming true: The one who ate bread at my table will stab me in the back. I'm telling you all this ahead of time, so that when it happens you'll believe I am who I say I am. Make sure you get this right: receiving someone I send is the same as receiving me, just as receiving me is the same as receiving the One who sent me."
After he said these things, Jesus became visibly upset, and then he told them why. "One of you is going to betray me."

The disciples looked around at one another, wondering who on earth he was talking about. One of the disciples, the one Jesus loved dearly, was leaning against him, his head on his shoulder. Peter motioned to him to ask who Jesus might mean. So, being the closest, he said, "Master, who?"

Jesus said, "The one I give this piece of bread to after I've dipped it." Then he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. As soon as the bread was in his hand, Satan entered him. "What you have to do," said Jesus, "do it. Do it and get it over with."

No one around the supper table knew why he said this to him. Some thought that since Judas was their treasurer, Jesus was telling him to buy what they needed for the Feast, or that he should give something to the poor.
Judas, with the piece of bread, left. It was night.
§A New Command

When he'd left, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is seen for who he is, and God is seen for who he is in him. The moment God is seen in him, God's glory will be on display. In glorifying him, he himself is glorified—glory all around!
"Children, I'm with you only a little while longer. You're going to look high and low for me. But just as I told the Jews, I'm telling you: 'Where I go, you can't come.'

"Let me give you a new command: love one another. Just as I loved you, you love one another. This is how everyone will recognize that you're my disciples—when they see the love you have for each other."
Simon Peter asked, "Master, just where are you going?" Jesus answered, "You can't follow me now where I'm going. You will follow later."
"Master," said Peter, "why can't I follow now? I'll lay down my life for you!"
"Really? You'll lay down your life for me? The truth is, before the rooster crows, you'll deny me three times."

title: The Way, The Truth, and The Promise
paragraphs: §The Road

"Don't let this shake you. You trust God, don't you? Trust me. There's plenty of room for you in my Father's house. If that weren't true, would I have told you I'm going to get a room ready for you? And since I'm going to get your room ready, I'll come back and get you, so you can live where I live. And you already know the road I'm taking."
Thomas said, "Master, we have no idea where you're going. How can we know the road?"

Jesus said, "I am the Road—and the Truth, and the Life. No one gets to the Father except through me. If you really knew me, you'd know my Father too. From now on, you do know him. You've even seen him!"
Philip said, "Master, show us the Father, and we'll be satisfied."

"You've been with me all this time, Philip, and you still don't get it? To see me is to see the Father. So how can you ask, 'Where is the Father?' Don't you believe I'm in the Father and the Father is in me? The words I speak to you aren't just words. I don't make them up on my own. The Father who lives in me turns each word into a divine act.

"Believe me: I am in my Father, and my Father is in me. If you can't believe that, believe what you see—these works. The person who trusts me will not only do what I'm doing but even greater things, because I, on my way to the Father, am giving you the same work to do that I've been doing. You can count on it. From now on, whatever you ask in line with who I am and what I'm doing, I'll do it. That's how the Father will be seen for who he is in the Son. I mean it. Whatever you ask in this way, I'll do.
§The Spirit of Truth

"If you love me, show it by doing what I've told you. I'll talk to the Father, and he'll give you another Friend, so you'll always have someone with you. This Friend is the Spirit of Truth. The godless world can't receive him, because it has no eyes to see him and doesn't know what to look for. But you already know him, because he's been staying with you—and he'll even be in you!

"I won't leave you orphaned. I'm coming back. In just a little while the world won't see me anymore, but you will see me—because I am alive, and you're about to come alive. At that moment you'll know for certain that I'm in my Father, and you're in me, and I'm in you.
"The person who knows my commands and keeps them—that's who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and make myself clear to him."
Judas (not Iscariot) said, "Master, why are you about to reveal yourself to us but not to the world?"

"Because a loveless world," said Jesus, "is a blind world. If anyone loves me, he'll carefully keep my word, and my Father will love him—and we'll move right into the neighborhood! Not loving me means not keeping my words. The message you're hearing isn't mine. It's the message of the Father who sent me.

"I'm telling you these things while I'm still living with you. The Friend, the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send at my request, will make everything clear to you. He'll remind you of everything I've told you. I'm leaving you well and whole—that's my parting gift to you. Peace. I don't leave you the way you're used to being left—feeling abandoned, empty. So don't be upset. Don't be distressed.
"You've heard me say, 'I'm going away, and I'm coming back.' If you loved me, you'd be glad I'm on my way to the Father, because the Father is the goal and purpose of my life.

"I've told you this ahead of time, before it happens, so that when it does happen, the confirmation will deepen your belief in me. I won't be talking with you much longer like this, because the ruler of this godless world is about to attack. But don't worry—he has nothing on me, no claim on me. But so the world will know how completely I love the Father, I'm carrying out my Father's instructions down to the last detail." Get up. Let's go. It's time to leave here.
