title: The Vine, The Branches, and the Haters
paragraphs: §The Vine and the Branches

"I am the Real Vine, and my Father is the Farmer. He cuts off every branch of mine that doesn't bear grapes. And every branch that does bear grapes, he prunes back so it will bear even more. You are already pruned by the message I have spoken.
"Live in me. Make your home in me, just as I do in you. Just as a branch can't bear grapes by itself but only by being joined to the vine, you can't bear fruit unless you're joined with me.

"I am the Vine, you are the branches. When you're joined with me and I with you—the relationship intimate and organic—the harvest is sure to be abundant. Separated, you can't produce a thing. Anyone who separates from me is deadwood, gathered up and thrown on the bonfire. But if you make yourselves at home with me and my words are at home in you, you can be sure that whatever you ask will be heard and acted on. This is how my Father shows who he is—when you produce grapes, when you mature as my disciples.

"I've loved you the way my Father has loved me. Make yourselves at home in my love. If you keep my commands, you'll stay intimately at home in my love. That's what I've done—kept my Father's commands and made myself at home in his love.

"I've told you these things for a purpose: so my joy can be your joy, and your joy fully mature. This is my command: love one another the way I loved you. This is the very best way to love. Put your life on the line for your friends. You are my friends when you do what I command you. I'm no longer calling you servants, because servants don't understand what their master is thinking and planning. No—I've named you friends, because I've let you in on everything I've heard from the Father.
"You didn't choose me, remember—I chose you, and put you in the world to bear fruit, fruit that won't spoil. As fruit-bearers, whatever you ask the Father in connection with me, he gives you.
"But remember the root command: love one another.
§Hated by the World

"If you find the godless world hating you, remember it started by hating me. If you lived on the world's terms, the world would love you as one of its own. But since I picked you to live on God's terms and not the world's, the world is going to hate you.

"When that happens, remember this: servants don't get better treatment than their masters. If they beat on me, they'll certainly beat on you. If they did what I told them, they'll do what you tell them.

"They're going to do all these things to you because of how they treated me—because they don't know the One who sent me. If I hadn't come and told them all this in plain language, it wouldn't be so bad. As it is, they have no excuse. Hate me, hate my Father—it's all the same. If I hadn't done what I've done among them—works no one has ever done—they wouldn't be to blame. But they saw the God-signs and hated anyway, both me and my Father. Interesting—they've confirmed the truth of their own Scriptures, where it's written, 'They hated me for no good reason.'

"When the Friend I plan to send you from the Father comes—the Spirit of Truth coming from the Father—he will confirm everything about me. You, too, from your side must give your confirming evidence, since you've been in this with me from the start."

title: Grief Turns to Explosive Joy
paragraphs: §Hated by the World

"I've told you these things to get you ready for the rough times ahead. They're going to throw you out of the meeting places. There'll even come a time when anyone who kills you will think he's doing God a favor. They'll do these things because they never really understood the Father. I've told you these things so that when the time comes and they start in on you, you'll be warned and ready.
§The Friend Will Come

"I didn't tell you this earlier, because I was with you every day. But now I'm on my way to the One who sent me. Not one of you has asked, 'Where are you going?' Instead, the longer I've talked, the sadder you've become. So let me say it again, this truth: it's better for you that I leave. If I don't leave, the Friend won't come. But if I go, I'll send him to you.

"When he comes, he'll expose how wrong the godless world's ideas of sin, righteousness, and judgment are. He'll show them that refusing to believe in me is their basic sin; that righteousness comes from above, where I am with the Father, out of their sight and control; that judgment happens as the ruler of this godless world is put on trial and convicted.

"I still have many things to tell you, but you can't handle them now. But when the Friend comes—the Spirit of Truth—he'll take you by the hand and guide you into all the truth there is. He won't draw attention to himself, but will make sense of what's about to happen and, really, of everything I've done and said. He'll honor me; he'll take from me and deliver it to you. Everything the Father has is also mine. That's why I've said, 'He takes from me and delivers to you.'
"In a day or so you're not going to see me, but then in another day or so you will see me."
§Joy Like a River Overflowing

That stirred up a hornet's nest of questions among the disciples: "What's he talking about—'In a day or so you're not going to see me, but then in another day or so you will see me'? And, 'Because I'm on my way to the Father'? What is this 'day or so'? We don't know what he's talking about."

Jesus knew they were dying to ask him what he meant, so he said, "Are you trying to figure out among yourselves what I meant when I said, 'In a day or so you're not going to see me, but then in another day or so you will see me'? Then get this firmly into your minds: you're going to be in deep mourning while the godless world throws a party. You'll be sad, very sad—but your sadness will turn into gladness.

"When a woman gives birth, she goes through a hard time—no getting around it. But when the baby is born, there's joy in the birth. This new life in the world wipes out the memory of the pain. The sadness you have right now is like that pain, but the coming joy is similar too. When I see you again, you'll be full of joy, and it'll be a joy no one can steal from you. You won't be so full of questions anymore.

"This is what I want you to do: ask the Father for whatever fits with the things I've revealed to you. Ask in my name, in line with my will, and he'll certainly give it to you. Your joy will be a river overflowing its banks!

"I've used figures of speech in telling you these things. Soon I'll drop the figures and tell you about the Father in plain language. Then you can make your requests directly to him, in connection with this life I've revealed to you. I won't keep making requests of the Father on your behalf. I won't need to. Because you've gone out on a limb, committing yourselves to love and trust me, believing I came straight from the Father, the Father loves you directly. First, I left the Father and came into the world; now I leave the world and go to the Father."

His disciples said, "Finally! You're giving it to us straight, in plain talk—no more figures of speech. Now we know you know everything—it all comes together in you. You won't have to put up with our questions anymore. We're convinced you came from God."

Jesus answered them, "Do you finally believe? Actually, you're about to run for it—saving your own skins and abandoning me. But I'm not abandoned. The Father is with me. I've told you all this so that, trusting me, you'll be unshakable and sure, deeply at peace. In this godless world you'll keep running into difficulties. But take heart! I've conquered the world."

title: The Epic High Priestly Prayer
paragraphs: §Jesus' Prayer for His Followers

Jesus said these things. Then, raising his eyes in prayer, he said: Father, it's time. Show the bright splendor of your Son, so the Son in turn can show your bright splendor. You put him in charge of everything human, so he could give real, eternal life to everyone in his care. And this is the real, eternal life: that they know you, the one and only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent. I glorified you on earth by completing, down to the last detail, what you assigned me to do. And now, Father, glorify me with your very own splendor—the very splendor I had in your presence before there was a world.

I spelled out your character in detail to the men and women you gave me. They were yours first; then you gave them to me, and they've now done what you said. They know now, beyond any doubt, that everything you gave me comes straight from you—because the message you gave me, I gave to them. And they received it, and were convinced that I came from you. They believed you sent me. I pray for them. I'm not praying for the God-rejecting world, but for those you gave me, for they are yours by right. Everything mine is yours, and yours mine, and my life is on display in them. I'm no longer going to be visible in the world; they'll continue in the world while I return to you. Holy Father, guard them as they live out this life you gave as a gift through me, so they can be one heart and mind, just as we are one heart and mind. As long as I was with them, I guarded them in living out the life you gave through me; I even posted a lookout. And not one of them got away—except the rebel bent on destruction (the exception that proved the rule of Scripture).

Now I'm returning to you. I'm saying these things where the world can hear, so my people can experience my joy completed in them. I gave them your word; the godless world hated them because of it, because they didn't join the world's ways—just as I didn't join the world's ways. I'm not asking you to take them out of the world, but to guard them from the Evil One. They are no more defined by the world than I am defined by the world. Make them holy—set apart—with the truth; your word is truth that sets apart. Just as you gave me a mission in the world, I give them a mission in the world. I'm setting myself apart for their sakes, so they'll be truth-set-apart in their mission.

I'm praying not only for them, but also for those who will believe in me because of them and their witness about me. The goal is for all of them to become one heart and mind—just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so they can be one heart and mind with us. Then the world might believe that you really did send me. The same glory you gave me, I gave them, so they'll be as unified and together as we are—I in them and you in me. Then they'll be mature in this oneness, and give the godless world proof that you've sent me and loved them the same way you've loved me.

Father, I want those you gave me to be with me, right where I am, so they can see my glory—the splendor you gave me, having loved me long before there ever was a world. Righteous Father, the world has never known you, but I have known you, and these disciples know that you sent me on this mission. I have made your very being known to them—who you are and what you do—and I keep making it known, so that your love for me can be in them exactly as I am in them.

title: The Garden Ambush and the Cowardly Governor
paragraphs: §Seized in the Garden at Night
Jesus, having prayed this prayer, left with his disciples and crossed the Kidron brook to a place where there was a garden. He and his disciples went into it.

Judas, his betrayer, knew the place, because Jesus and his disciples went there often. So Judas led the way to the garden, and the Roman soldiers and police sent by the high priests and Pharisees followed. They arrived with lanterns and torches and swords. Jesus, knowing by now everything that was crashing down on him, went out and met them. He said, "Who are you looking for?" They answered, "Jesus the Nazarene."
He said, "That's me." The soldiers recoiled, completely thrown off. Judas, his betrayer, stood out like a sore thumb.
Jesus asked again, "Who are you looking for?" They answered, "Jesus the Nazarene."
"I told you," said Jesus, "that's me. I'm the one. So if it's me you're after, let these others go." (This confirmed the words in his prayer: "I didn't lose one of those you gave me.")
Just then Simon Peter, who was carrying a sword, pulled it from its sheath and struck the Chief Priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus ordered Peter, "Put your sword away. Do you think for a minute I'm not going to drink this cup the Father gave me?"

Then the Roman soldiers under their commander, joined by the Jewish police, seized Jesus and tied him up. They took him first to Annas, father-in-law of Caiaphas. Caiaphas was the Chief Priest that year. It was Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was to their advantage for one man to die for the people.

Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. That other disciple was known to the Chief Priest, so he went in with Jesus to the Chief Priest's courtyard. Peter had to stay outside. Then the other disciple went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and got Peter in.
The young woman at the door said to Peter, "Aren't you one of this man's disciples?" He said, "No, I'm not."
The servants and police had made a fire because of the cold and were huddled around it warming themselves. Peter stood with them, trying to get warm.
§The Interrogation

Annas interrogated Jesus about his disciples and his teaching. Jesus answered, "I've spoken openly in public. I've taught regularly in meeting places and the Temple, where all the Jews gather. Everything has been out in the open. I've said nothing in secret. So why are you treating me like a traitor? Ask the people who've been listening to me. They know well what I've said. My teachings have all been aboveboard."
When he said this, one of the policemen standing there slapped Jesus across the face, saying, "How dare you talk to the Chief Priest like that!"
Jesus replied, "If I've said something wrong, prove it. But if I've spoken the plain truth, why all this slapping?"
Then Annas sent him, still tied up, to the Chief Priest Caiaphas.
Meanwhile, Simon Peter was back at the fire, still trying to get warm. The others there said to him, "Aren't you one of his disciples?" He denied it: "Not me."
One of the Chief Priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Didn't I see you in the garden with him?"
Again Peter denied it. Just then a rooster crowed.
§The King of the Jews

They then led Jesus from Caiaphas to the Roman governor's palace. It was early morning. They didn't enter the palace themselves, because they didn't want to be disqualified from eating the Passover. So Pilate came out to them and asked, "What charge are you bringing against this man?"
They said, "If he hadn't been doing something evil, do you think we'd be here bothering you?"
Pilate said, "Take him yourselves. Judge him by your law." The Jews said, "We're not allowed to kill anyone." (This would confirm Jesus' word about how he would die.)
Pilate went back into the palace and called for Jesus. He said, "Are you the 'King of the Jews'?"
Jesus answered, "Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you this about me?"
Pilate said, "Do I look like a Jew? Your people and your high priests handed you over to me. What did you do?"

"My kingdom," said Jesus, "isn't made of what you see around you. If it were, my followers would fight so I wouldn't be handed over to the Jews. But I'm not that kind of king—not the world's kind of king."

Then Pilate said, "So, are you a king or not?" Jesus answered, "You tell me. Because I am King, I was born and came into the world so I could testify to the truth. Everyone who cares about truth, who has any feeling for the truth, recognizes my voice."

Pilate said, "What is truth?" Then he went back out to the Jews and told them, "I find nothing wrong with this man. It's your custom that I pardon one prisoner at Passover. Do you want me to pardon the 'King of the Jews'?"
They shouted back, "Not this one—Barabbas!" Barabbas was a Jewish freedom fighter.

title: The Torture, The Cross, and The Tomb
paragraphs: §The Thorn Crown of the King

So Pilate took Jesus and had him whipped. The soldiers braided a crown from thorns and set it on his head, threw a purple robe over him, and came up to him saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" Then they greeted him with slaps to the face.

Pilate went back out again and said to them, "I'm presenting him to you, but I want you to know I don't find him guilty of any crime." Just then Jesus came out, wearing the thorn crown and the purple robe. Pilate announced, "Here he is: the Man."
When the high priests and police saw him, they shouted wildly, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate told them, "You take him. You crucify him. I find nothing wrong with him."
The Jews answered, "We have a law, and by that law he must die, because he claimed to be the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he got even more scared. He went back into the palace and said to Jesus, "Where did you come from?" Jesus gave no answer.
Pilate said, "You won't talk? Don't you know I have the authority to pardon you, and the authority to—crucify you?"
Jesus said, "You don't have a shred of authority over me except what's been given to you from above. That's why the one who handed me over to you has committed a far greater wrong."
At this, Pilate tried hard to set him free, but the Jews shouted him down: "If you let this man go, you're no friend of Caesar's. Anyone who sets himself up as 'king' defies Caesar."

When Pilate heard those words, he led Jesus outside. He sat down at the judgment seat in the area called Stone Court (in Hebrew, Gabbatha). It was the preparation day for Passover. The hour was noon. Pilate said to the Jews, "Here is your king."
They shouted back, "Kill him! Kill him! Crucify him!" Pilate said, "Am I supposed to crucify your king?" The high priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar."

Pilate gave in to their demand. He handed him over to be crucified. They took Jesus away. Carrying his cross, Jesus went out to the place called Skull Hill (in Hebrew, Golgotha), where they crucified him—and with him two others, one on each side, Jesus in the middle. Pilate wrote a sign and had it put on the cross. It read: jesus the nazarene the king of the jews.
§The Crucifixion

Many of the Jews read the sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was right next to the city. It was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek. The Jewish high priests objected. "Don't write," they said to Pilate, "'The King of the Jews.' Write, 'This man said, "I am the King of the Jews."'"
Pilate said, "What I've written, I've written."

When they crucified him, the Roman soldiers took his clothes and divided them four ways—a fourth to each soldier. But his robe was seamless, a single piece of weaving, so they said to each other, "Let's not tear it. Let's throw dice to see who gets it." This confirmed the Scripture that said, "They divided my clothes among them and threw dice for my coat." (The soldiers proved the Scriptures right!)

While the soldiers were looking after themselves, Jesus' mother, his aunt, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene stood at the foot of the cross. Jesus saw his mother and the disciple he loved standing near her. He said to his mother, "Woman, here is your son." Then to the disciple, "Here is your mother." From that moment the disciple took her as his own mother.
Jesus, seeing that everything had been finished, so that the Scripture record would also be complete, then said, "I'm thirsty."

A jug of sour wine was standing nearby. Someone put a sponge soaked with the wine on a javelin and lifted it to his mouth. After he took the wine, Jesus said, "It's done… finished." Bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.

Then the Jews—since it was the day of Sabbath preparation, and they didn't want the bodies to stay on the crosses over the Sabbath (it was a high holy day that year)—asked Pilate to have their legs broken to speed up death, and the bodies taken down. So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man crucified with Jesus, and then the other. When they got to Jesus, they saw he was already dead, so they didn't break his legs. One of the soldiers stabbed him in the side with his spear. Blood and water poured out.
The eyewitness to these events has given an accurate report. He saw it himself and is telling the truth, so that you, too, will believe.
These things happened to confirm the Scripture: "Not a bone in his body was broken," and the other Scripture that reads, "They will stare at the one they pierced."

After all this, Joseph of Arimathea (he was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, because he was afraid of the Jews) asked Pilate for Jesus' body. Pilate gave permission. So Joseph came and took the body.

Nicodemus, who had first come to Jesus at night, now came in broad daylight, carrying a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds. They took Jesus' body and, following the Jewish burial custom, wrapped it in linen with the spices. There was a garden near the place where he was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever been placed. So, because it was Sabbath preparation for the Jews and the tomb was close by, they laid Jesus in it.

title: The Empty Tomb and Doubting Thomas
paragraphs: §Resurrection!

Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw the stone moved away from the entrance. She ran at once to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one Jesus loved, gasping for breath. "They took the Master from the tomb. We don't know where they've put him."

Peter and the other disciple left immediately for the tomb. They ran neck and neck. The other disciple got to the tomb first, outrunning Peter. Stooping to look in, he saw the linen cloths lying there, but he didn't go in. Simon Peter arrived after him, entered the tomb, and observed the linen cloths lying there—and the cloth that had covered his head, not lying with the linen cloths but separate, neatly folded by itself. Then the other disciple, the one who'd gotten there first, went into the tomb, took one look at the evidence, and believed. No one yet knew from the Scripture that he had to rise from the dead. Then the disciples went back home.

But Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping. As she wept, she knelt to look into the tomb and saw two angels sitting there, dressed in white—one at the head, the other at the foot of where Jesus' body had been laid. They said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?"
"They took my Master," she said, "and I don't know where they put him." After she said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there. But she didn't recognize him.
Jesus spoke to her: "Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?" Thinking he was the gardener, she said, "Sir, if you took him away, tell me where you put him so I can take care of him."
Jesus said, "Mary." Turning to face him, she said in Hebrew, "Rabboni!"—meaning "Teacher!"
Jesus said, "Don't cling to me, for I haven't yet ascended to the Father. Go to my brothers and tell them, 'I ascend to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.'"
Mary Magdalene went, telling the news to the disciples: "I've seen the Master!" And she told them everything he'd said to her.
§To Believe

Later that day, the disciples had gathered together but, fearful of the Jews, had locked all the doors in the house. Jesus came in, stood among them, and said, "Peace to you." Then he showed them his hands and his side.
The disciples, seeing the Master with their own eyes, were awestruck. Jesus repeated his greeting: "Peace to you. Just as the Father sent me, I send you."

Then he took a deep breath and breathed into them. "Receive the Holy Spirit," he said. "If you forgive someone's sins, they're gone for good. If you don't forgive sins, what are you going to do with them?"

But Thomas, sometimes called the Twin, one of the Twelve, wasn't with them when Jesus came. The other disciples told him, "We saw the Master." But he said, "Unless I see the nail holes in his hands, put my finger in the nail holes, and stick my hand in his side, I won't believe it."
Eight days later, his disciples were in the room again. This time Thomas was with them. Jesus came through the locked doors, stood among them, and said, "Peace to you."
Then he focused on Thomas. "Take your finger and examine my hands. Take your hand and stick it in my side. Don't be unbelieving. Believe."
Thomas said, "My Master! My God!"
Jesus said, "So you believe because you've seen with your own eyes. Even better blessings are in store for those who believe without seeing."

Jesus did far more God-revealing signs than are written down in this book. These are written down so you'll believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God—and by believing, have real, eternal life in the way he personally revealed it.

title: Breakfast on the Beach and The Comeback
paragraphs: §Fishing

After this, Jesus appeared again to the disciples, this time at the Tiberias Sea (the Sea of Galilee). This is how he did it: Simon Peter, Thomas (nicknamed "Twin"), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the Zebedee brothers, and two other disciples were together. Simon Peter announced, "I'm going fishing."
The rest of them said, "We're going with you." They went out and got in the boat. They caught nothing that night. When the sun came up, Jesus was standing on the beach, but they didn't recognize him.
Jesus called out to them, "Good morning! Did you catch anything for breakfast?" They answered, "No."
He said, "Throw the net off the right side of the boat and see what happens." They did what he said. All of a sudden there were so many fish, they weren't strong enough to pull the net in.

Then the disciple Jesus loved said to Peter, "It's the Master!" When Simon Peter realized it was the Master, he threw on some clothes—he'd stripped down for work—and dove into the sea. The other disciples came in by boat, since they weren't far from land, about a hundred yards, pulling the net full of fish. When they got out of the boat, they saw a charcoal fire already laid, with fish and bread cooking on it.
Jesus said, "Bring some of the fish you've just caught." Simon Peter joined them and pulled the net to shore—153 big fish! And even with all those fish, the net didn't rip.
Jesus said, "Breakfast is ready." Not one of the disciples dared ask, "Who are you?" They knew it was the Master.
Jesus then took the bread and gave it to them. He did the same with the fish. This was now the third time Jesus had shown himself alive to the disciples since being raised from the dead.
§Do You Love Me?
After breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Master, you know I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."
He asked a second time, "Simon, son of John, do you love me?" "Yes, Master, you know I love you." Jesus said, "Shepherd my sheep."

Then a third time: "Simon, son of John, do you love me?" Peter was upset that he asked a third time, "Do you love me?" So he answered, "Master, you know everything there is to know. You've got to know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my sheep. I'm telling you the straight truth now: when you were young, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you get old, you'll stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you don't want to go." (He said this to hint at the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God.) Then he commanded, "Follow me."
Turning around, Peter noticed the disciple Jesus loved following right behind. When Peter saw him, he asked Jesus, "Master, what's going to happen to him?"

Jesus said, "If I want him to live until I come again, what's that to you? You—follow me." That's how the rumor got out among the brothers that this disciple wouldn't die. But that's not what Jesus said. He simply said, "If I want him to live until I come again, what's that to you?"
This is the same disciple who was an eyewitness to all these things and wrote them down. And we all know his eyewitness account is reliable and accurate.
There are so many other things Jesus did. If they were all written down, each one, one by one, I can't imagine a world big enough to hold such a library of books.
